tracks.narration: A weight on a string — pull it sideways and let go. What sets the rhythm of its swing?
Hang a mass from a string of length L. Pull it to angle theta. Gravity pulls straight down, but only the tangential component, minus m g sine theta, restores it toward vertical.

For small swings, sine theta is approximately theta. The equation of motion becomes the second derivative of theta plus g over L theta equals zero — exactly the spring equation, with omega zero equal to the square root of g over L.
The period is two pi over omega zero — so T equals two pi times the square root of L over g. Notice what is missing: the mass.
Heavier bob, lighter bob — same length swings to the same beat. Gravity sets the metronome.
